name: Five Nights at Freddy's: Security Breach

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate with a 30 fps cap gives the smoothest pacing for this style of slow-burn horror gameplay; medium textures keep the Pizzaplex looking reasonable without overwhelming the shared memory pool. Drop shadows to Low if frame rate dips in the main atrium.

profiles.Summary: Five Nights at Freddy's: Security Breach is a demanding Unreal Engine 4 horror-adventure that sits right at the edge of the Steam Deck's capabilities, requiring low settings and FSR upscaling to maintain a stable 30 fps in the busiest areas of the Pizzaplex. The game is Steam Deck Verified and runs under Proton without major setup, though its heavy environment and lighting demands mean high settings are not realistic on the Deck's hardware.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1050 Ti class, matching the Deck's GPU) and Unreal Engine 4 behaviour on similar hardware. On first launch, check frame rate in the main Pizzaplex atrium — that is the heaviest area — and step down to Max Battery settings if it cannot hold 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at sub-native resolution with FSR on the Deck side reduces GPU load significantly; locking to 30 fps with a low TDP keeps thermals and fan noise down for longer sessions. In-game Resolution Scale should be kept low since FSR on the Deck handles upscaling.

KnownIssues: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC requirements and Deck hardware capabilities.
The Pizzaplex hub and large open areas are GPU-heavy and may cause frame drops even at low settings.
Shader compilation stutters on first launch are common with Unreal Engine 4 games under Proton.
The game requires ~80 GB of storage, which may require an SD card on base-model Decks.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at full 15 W TDP with the GPU at max clock squeezes the most out of the Deck, but frame rate will dip into the low 30s in the busiest Pizzaplex areas — expect inconsistency rather than a locked 40. If stutters are persistent, drop Shadow Quality to Low and Effects Quality to Low.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives the smoothest feel the Deck can reliably sustain in this game; FSR from 1024x640 keeps image quality acceptable while relieving GPU pressure. Shadows and ambient occlusion are the biggest performance drains and are kept low or off.

profiles.Summary: Five Nights at Freddy's: Security Breach is a demanding Unreal Engine 4 horror-adventure that sits right at the Steam Deck's performance ceiling — the minimum GPU spec (GTX 1050 Ti) matches the Deck's GPU class, so expect 30–40 fps only at low/medium settings with upscaling. ProtonDB rates it gold, meaning it runs with minor issues under Proton but may need some tweaking for stability.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1050 Ti, matching the Deck's GPU class) and general UE4 game behaviour on Deck. On your first run, check frame rate in the main Pizzaplex atrium — if it drops below 30 fps consistently, move to Max Battery settings or lower shadow quality further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 and a low TDP cap keeps thermals and draw down for extended sessions. If the 30 fps cap feels unstable in the busiest areas, try dropping Overall Quality to Very Low.

KnownIssues: Some players report occasional crashes or freezes, especially in busier areas of the Pizzaplex
Performance can drop significantly in large open areas with many animatronics on screen
Audio sync issues have been reported under certain Proton versions
No native Linux build — runs via Proton, which may introduce minor graphical glitches

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at native 1280x800 with medium settings and max GPU clock pushes the Deck to its limits — expect dips below 45 fps in the most demanding Pizzaplex sections. Battery life will be short; this profile is best for docked or plugged-in play.
